correctness.rationale: For every odd N>=3 and finite J_i>0, phase closure implies exact energy identity (1). Telescoping complex unit phases and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz yield the sharp global bound (2). Equality is rigid because at least two other bonds prevent simultaneous nonzero triangle and weighted-CS equality. Above the threshold, an admissible analytic perturbation has negative quadratic energy change. The coefficient is sharp by its perturbative limit. Reconstructed normalization E=-sum J+F and both threshold boundaries; local numerical 96+30 tests are supplementary only.

value.rationale: Unknown general exact rigidity/canting boundary for a heterogeneous classical XY loop is a natural ground-state design quantity for frustrated spin rings and pi-flux phase networks. It determines whether all frustration can sit on a weakest link even with multiple nonuniform exchange strengths, makes the remaining edges a series stiffness, resolves the exact critical equality, and supplies a quantitatively sharp global energy penalty. This is stronger than the previously known single-defect alpha threshold and not merely numerical novelty.
